cues.en: So we're here for
cues.zh: 我们今天来到这里是为了

cues.en: oral history of Avi Tovanian, and it is Tovanian. Tovanian. I'll restart it with it. Thank Avi
cues.zh: 记录 Avi Tovanian 的口述历史，是叫 Tovanian 对吧。Tovanian。我重新录一下这段。感谢 Avi

cues.en: Tovanian, and it's February 21. And I'm John Markoff,
cues.zh: Tovanian，今天是2月21日。我是 John Markoff，

cues.en: and Hansen Su is to my left, and David Brock is to my right. And on we go. So can we start by
cues.zh: 我左边是 Hansen Su，右边是 David Brock。我们这就开始。首先能不能请你

cues.en: having you tell us where and when you were born? Sure. I was born in Portland, Maine, back east in 1961.
cues.zh: 跟我们讲讲你是在何时何地出生的？没问题。我1961年出生在美东的缅因州波特兰。

cues.en: Okay. And
cues.zh: 好的。那

cues.en: can you tell
cues.zh: 你能讲讲

cues.en: us something about your family and how your family came to to Maine and,
cues.zh: 你的家庭背景，以及你们家是怎么来到缅因州的吗？

cues.en: you know, a little bit of their origin.
cues.zh: 也就是聊聊你的家族渊源。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 这个嘛，

cues.en: I'm a 100% Armenian. Both of my parents are Armenian,
cues.zh: 我是百分之百的亚美尼亚人。我父母都是亚美尼亚人，

cues.en: and both of their parents, all of my grandparents, came over in the early nineteen hundreds from Armenia,
cues.zh: 他们的父母，也就是我的祖父母和外祖父母，都是在20世纪初从亚美尼亚过来的，

cues.en: as part of the,
cues.zh: 主要是因为当时……

cues.en: you know, war with the Turks.
cues.zh: 也就是和土耳其人的战争。

cues.en: I should know more about that than I actually do. Certainly heard a lot of stories about that when I was younger and mostly forgotten them.
cues.zh: 关于那段历史我其实应该多了解一些的。小时候确实听过很多相关的故事，但大多都忘了。

cues.en: So anyway, my grandparents came across literally on the boat.
cues.zh: 总之，我的祖辈当年真的就是坐船漂洋过海过来的。

cues.en: They had children.
cues.zh: 后来他们有了孩子。

cues.en: My dad my dad's family went to Portland, Maine. My mom's family went to Worcester, Massachusetts. Massachusetts.
cues.zh: 我父亲……我父亲一家去了缅因州波特兰。我母亲一家去了马萨诸塞州伍斯特。伍斯特。

cues.en: Somewhere along the way, they met each other. Don't know how that happened.
cues.zh: 后来的某个时候，他们相遇了。我也不知道他们是怎么认识的。

cues.en: They got married, I was their oldest son. And was Armenian spoken in the household when you were growing up? It was a little bit.
cues.zh: 他们结了婚，我是他们的大儿子。你小时候家里会说亚美尼亚语吗？会说一点点。

cues.en: My parents were both fluent in Armenia... Armenian.
cues.zh: 我父母都能说一口流利的亚美尼……亚美尼亚语。

cues.en: They would usually use it when they didn't want us kids to know what they were saying.
cues.zh: 他们通常只在不想让我们这帮小孩子听懂的时候才讲。

cues.en: But we knew a few of the words ourselves, not enough to converse with them, but we could usually figure out what they were saying. Yeah. Yeah. And what did your parents do?
cues.zh: 但我们自己也懂一些词，不够和他们对话，但通常能弄明白他们在说什么。是啊。是啊。那你父母是做什么的？

cues.en: So my mom was some kind of bookkeeper
cues.zh: 我妈妈算是某种簿记员

cues.en: before she was married.
cues.zh: 在她结婚之前。

cues.en: When she got married, I think she gave up that career, just became a full time mom. I came pretty early on after they got married, and she had four boys, so we kept her busy. Uh-huh.
cues.zh: 结婚后，我想她放弃了那份职业，成了全职妈妈。他们结婚后没多久我就出生了，她生了四个男孩，所以我们让她很忙。嗯哼。

cues.en: My dad started out
cues.zh: 我爸爸一开始

cues.en: basically...
cues.zh: 基本上……

cues.en: Well, when he was very young, like
cues.zh: 嗯，在他很小的时候，大概

cues.en: Very poor family, obviously, coming from Armenia in Portland.
cues.zh: 很穷的家庭，显然，从波特兰的阿美尼亚来的。

cues.en: And he worked when he was very young and tried to also go to school. So he would... In Portland, he'd go down to the wharf in the morning,
cues.zh: 他很小就工作了，还努力上学。所以他会……在波特兰，他早上会去码头，

cues.en: like 3AM, 4AM when the fishing boats were coming in. He'd buy the fish from them, take them to the super markets, and try to make some money doing that. Then he'd go do a paper route and just anything that he could
cues.zh: 大概凌晨3点、4点渔船进港的时候。他从他们那买鱼，送到超市，试着这样赚点钱。然后他会去送报纸，只要能做的

cues.en: while still going to school.
cues.zh: 同时还在上学。

cues.en: He then went into the army for World War two. He was a machinist. He was always good with his hands.
cues.zh: 后来他参加了二战参军。他是个机械师。他一直很擅长动手。

cues.en: He was literally in the action, not on the front lines, but right behind.
cues.zh: 他确实在行动中，不在前线，但就在后面。

cues.en: As a machinist, he would go and fix tanks when they broke down or whatever else.
cues.zh: 作为机械师，他会去修坏掉的坦克或其他什么。

cues.en: Then he came back, and he was basically...
cues.zh: 然后他回来了，基本上……

cues.en: You he did jobs where he could use his hands for a while,
cues.zh: 他做了一阵子能用手的工作，

cues.en: working in machine shops,
cues.zh: 在机械车间工作，

cues.en: worked in a Christmas ornament factory for a while, if I recall correctly.
cues.zh: 如果我没记错的话，还在一家圣诞装饰品工厂工作过一段时间。

cues.en: And then he basically became an entrepreneur.
cues.zh: 然后他基本上就成了一名创业者。

cues.en: In the
cues.zh: 在

cues.en: late fifties,
cues.zh: 五十多岁末期，

cues.en: which, of course, is before I was born,
cues.zh: 当然，那是在我出生之前，

cues.en: he saw an opportunity or he saw a movement of drive in theaters.
cues.zh: 他看到了一个机会，或者看到了影院里一股驱动力。

cues.en: And so he bought some land just outside of Portland and built a drive in theater, which exists today and is still family business. Oh, wow.
cues.zh: 于是他在波特兰郊外买了块地，建了一家汽车影院；这家影院如今还在，仍然是家族生意。哦，哇。

cues.en: He then, in the sixties,
cues.zh: 他在六十年代，

cues.en: while also operating the
cues.zh: 同时还要操作

cues.en: drive in theater, bought a bowling alley out of bankruptcy
cues.zh: 汽车影院，从破产中买下了一个保龄球馆。

cues.en: and rebuilt that business and turned it around.
cues.zh: 并重建了那项业务，使其扭亏为盈。

cues.en: I spent many hours working in that bowling alley myself.
cues.zh: 我自己也在那家保龄球馆工作过很长时间。

cues.en: And then as my younger brothers were getting to the age where they would go out and get jobs and stuff, he built a business beside the bowling alley, which was, at that time, a retail boat business,
cues.zh: 后来，等我弟弟们到了该出去找工作之类的年纪，他在保龄球馆旁边做起了生意，当时那是一家零售船艇的店，

cues.en: which then got morphed into other
cues.zh: 后来演变成了其他

cues.en: fun toys like snowmobiles,
cues.zh: 像雪地摩托这样的有趣玩具，

cues.en: motorcycles,
cues.zh: 摩托车，

cues.en: things like that, which a couple of my brothers still run. Your dad's sort of entrepreneurial
cues.zh: 诸如此类的东西，我的几个兄弟还在经营。你爸爸有点创业精神

cues.en: gene,
cues.zh: 基因，

cues.en: it's interesting. He started sort of as blue collar worker. Yes. And... But going back, do you know if there was an entrepreneurial history in the in the family in Armenia? What
cues.zh: 这挺有意思。他最初算是蓝领工人。是的。而且……但往回看，你知道亚美尼亚的家族里有没有创业的历史吗？什么

cues.en: pushed him toward business?
cues.zh: 这是要把他推向商业吗？

cues.en: You know, I I really don't know.
cues.zh: 说实话，我真不知道。

cues.en: I mean, it's... It was so long ago, and we lost him about thirty years ago. So it's been a while since I've heard any of the stories. He,
cues.zh: 我是说，那都是很久以前的事了，他大约三十年前就去世了。所以我已经很久没听过那些故事了。他，

cues.en: you know, he grew up in the age himself where you had to work hard just to put food on the table, and he was helping put food on his family's table by doing that. And so I think he learned a lot from being in the army, especially in World War two.
cues.zh: 你知道，他成长的那个年代，光是把饭端上桌就得拼命干活，而他就是靠那份工作帮家里挣饭吃。所以我觉得，他在军队里学到了很多，尤其是在二战期间。

cues.en: And he was just always looking for ways to better his family's family's life. And
cues.zh: 而且他一直在寻找改善家庭生活的方法。 And

cues.en: so I think when he got to a certain point of
cues.zh: 所以我想，当他达到一定的

cues.en: affluence, if you will, I mean, by the time I was born and growing up, we were definitely middle class. Yeah.
cues.zh: 富裕程度时——我是说，到我出生和成长的年代，我们家已经确实是中产阶级了。是的。

cues.en: You know, by working hard for many years, earning salary, and I'm sure saving it like crazy.
cues.zh: 你知道，通过多年的努力工作、赚取薪水，我敢肯定他还拼命地存钱。

cues.en: I think he thought he could take a little more risk, which was, you know, building the drive in theater to get beyond just having the regular nine to five type job. But he was he was he was not just a typical even though he started out as a blue collar worker, was not typical. I remember when I was younger, he taught me about how the stock market worked, which I thought was... You know, even back then, not many people even invested in the stock market. You had the Wall Street Journal with the, you know, the quotes in the back of the paper every single day. It was only when you got stock quotes. But he was into that, and he'd show it to me. So he was interested in these other things beyond just the blue the blue collar type stuff. Yeah.
cues.zh: 我想他觉得可以冒一点险了，那就是建汽车影院，而不只是满足于朝九晚五的普通工作。但他可不是一般人——虽然他起步是个蓝领工人，但绝不平庸。我记得小时候，他教我股票市场是怎么运作的，我觉得这……你知道，即使在那个年代，也没什么人投资股票。每天都有《华尔街日报》，报纸背面印着报价。那时候只有股票报价栏。但他热衷于这个，还会拿给我看。所以他的兴趣超越了蓝领工作的那些东西。是的。

cues.en: Could you say a little bit about your brothers? And what... Did they go in a technical direction, just sort of general? So I'm completely different than my brothers.
cues.zh: 能稍微说说你的兄弟们吗？他们……他们是走向了技术方向，还是普通的方向？我和我的兄弟们完全不同。

cues.en: They
cues.zh: 他们

cues.en: all went into the hands on type businesses themselves.
cues.zh: 都进入了自己动手实干型的行业。

cues.en: The... In fact, the three... I have three younger brothers. They all went in to the family business focusing
cues.zh: 那个……事实上，我有三个弟弟。他们都进入了家族企业，专注于

cues.en: on
cues.zh: 最初

cues.en: what would, again, start out as the boat business.
cues.zh: 以船舶业务起家的领域。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: my father actually died shortly after that was set up and operating,
cues.zh: 那套东西建好并运转起来后不久，我父亲就去世了，

cues.en: and he always had intended that that was something they could do with their lives, and they ended up doing that because he wasn't there to run anymore. So they kinda learned trial by fire on some of that. Well, I had one brother who worked building yachts for a while up at a place in Maine Yeah. And doing some other things like that. But two of them still do that today. Okay.
cues.zh: 他一直打算那是他们可以以此为事业的事业，而他们最终做成了这件事，因为父亲不在了，没办法再亲自经营。所以他们在很多方面算是硬着头皮、边干边学出来的。嗯，我有一个哥哥曾经在缅因州的一个地方造过一段时间的游艇，对。还做过一些类似的事情。不过另外两个哥哥至今仍在做这行。好的。

cues.en: And sort of characterize what the household was like, your home was like growing up. Were dinner table conversations lively? Sort of stylistically, what was the family like?
cues.zh: 能不能描述一下你成长过程中家里的氛围？餐桌上的谈话热闹吗？从风格上讲，你们家是个什么样的家庭？

cues.en: It was kind of crazy with four of us boys
cues.zh: 家里有我们四个男孩，挺闹腾的

cues.en: in in retrospect.
cues.zh: 现在回想起来。

cues.en: In some sense, it was a traditional Armenian family in that, you know, my mom was just a great cook, making traditional Armenian foods. And so, you know, nothing I would have appreciated at the time, of course, is just dinner.
cues.zh: 从某种意义上说，那是一个传统的亚美尼亚家庭，我妈妈手艺特别好，做传统的亚美尼亚菜。当然，那时候的我肯定不会珍惜这些，对我来说就是晚饭而已。

cues.en: Right? But
cues.zh: 对吧。但是

cues.en: it was it was something that I think was just really good for our upbringing. We always saw our dad as a hard worker,
cues.zh: 我觉得这对我们的成长真的很有好处。我们一直觉得父亲是个非常勤奋的人，

cues.en: going in early in the morning, coming back late at night.
cues.zh: 一大早就出门，深夜才回家。

cues.en: When we were old enough to know it was when he was rebuilding the bowling alley.
cues.zh: 等到我们大了才明白，那正是他在重新翻修保龄球馆的时候。

cues.en: My brothers and I were all close. We'd do things together all the time. We lived in a neighborhood that was friendly. Doors were always unlocked. We knew all the neighborhood kids. We'd go outside on the street, play kickball. We'd go down the street and find a big field and play baseball,
cues.zh: 我和哥哥们关系都很亲近，总是一起玩各种东西。我们住在一个很友好的社区，家家户户的门都不上锁，我们认识社区里所有的孩子。我们会跑到街上踢球，会沿着街找一片大空地打棒球，

cues.en: all those kinds of things. But this was this was typical of the sixties
cues.zh: 诸如此类的事情。但这在六十年代

cues.en: and early seventies. Yeah.
cues.zh: 和七十年代初是很典型的。是啊。

cues.en: You know, many evenings,
cues.zh: 你知道，很多个晚上，

cues.en: we'd all stay home and watch TV around
cues.zh: 我们都会待在家里，围着那台全家共用的电视看节目，

cues.en: the one family TV, like, again, like everybody did, sometimes with our TV dinners. I became a huge Star Trek fan then, right when it came out.
cues.zh: 就像大家当年那样，有时候还边吃电视晚餐。那时我成了《星际迷航》的超级粉丝，正好是它刚播出的时候。

cues.en: And so if if your brothers went into the family business, was there something... Did you go in a different direction?
cues.zh: 那么，如果你的兄弟们进了家族企业，是不是有什么……你走了不同的方向吗？

cues.en: I was always the different one. So when I was very young, they knew that I had an aptitude
cues.zh: 我一直是那个与众不同的人。所以我很小的时候，他们就知道我有天赋，

cues.en: for math is what it turned out to be. And so we'd all be in our station station wagon driving along,
cues.zh: 后来发现是数学方面的天赋。于是我们全家会坐上旅行车一路开着，

cues.en: the six of us, two parents and four kids, and my dad would be shouting
cues.zh: 我们六个人，两个大人四个孩子，我爸会大声喊出

cues.en: out math problems for me to solve.
cues.zh: 数学题让我解。

cues.en: And it would be, you know, multiplication tables or things like that.
cues.zh: 内容是乘法口诀表之类的。

cues.en: But,
cues.zh: 但是，

cues.en: you know, I was always the one that got good grades in school, and homework was easy, and it was it was more challenging for my brother. So it was always new... It it was always informally known
cues.zh: 你知道，我一直是学校里成绩好的那个，作业很轻松，对我兄弟来说则更有挑战。所以情况一直是……大家私下里都默认

cues.en: that I was kinda gonna be the one to go off and do something different. Yeah. Did you say you were the first? I was the oldest. Yes. Okay. Yes. And any idea what what... Where the aptitude for math came from?
cues.zh: 我大概会是那个出去做点不一样事情的人。是的。你说过你是第一个吗？我是老大。是的。好的。是的。那你知道这种……数学天赋是从哪来的吗？

cues.en: You know, I I think both my parents were pretty smart. I can't say that either one of them was particularly good at math, and I'm pretty sure that by the time I got to high school, I was doing more advanced math than they knew about because
cues.zh: 你知道，我觉得我父母都挺聪明的。我不能说他们中哪一个特别擅长数学，而且我很确定到我上高中的时候，我学的数学已经比他们知道的更高级了，因为

cues.en: they never helped me with homework, and I'm not sure they could have at the time.
cues.zh: 他们从没帮我做过作业，我也不确定他们那时候帮得上。

cues.en: It's just... I just got that gene from somewhere. Yeah. And and I had a love for it, and I think maybe that's part of the genetics too. Yeah.
cues.zh: 就是……我不知从哪儿继承了那种基因。是啊。而且我热爱它，我觉得也许这也是遗传的一部分。是啊。

cues.en: In that period in the sixties when you're growing up, religion and politics in your household, were there?
cues.zh: 在六十年代你成长的那段时期，你们家里有宗教和政治氛围吗？

cues.en: The
cues.zh: 那

cues.en: religion was minimal.
cues.zh: 宗教方面很少。

cues.en: My mom was somewhat religious from Massachusetts. She was a regular churchgoer.
cues.zh: 我妈来自Massachusetts，有点信教。她经常去教堂。

cues.en: And... But we'd all worn her down.
cues.zh: 而且……但我们把她磨得没脾气了。

cues.en: And the extent of her religion at that point was to try to get us to go to church for Christmas or Easter or something like that.
cues.zh: 那时她的宗教程度，也就是想让我们在圣诞节、复活节之类的时候去去教堂。

cues.en: Minimal politics.
cues.zh: 政治方面也很少。

cues.en: My dad leaned Republican as a businessman.
cues.zh: 我爸是商人，倾向共和党。

cues.en: He did run once for some city alderman position,
cues.zh: 他确实竞选过一次某个市参事职位，

cues.en: and he didn't know what he was doing, he didn't win. But he only he only did that once. Once. Yeah. Yeah.
cues.zh: 他也不知道自己在干什么，没赢。但他只只做过那一次。就一次。是啊。是啊。

cues.en: Was your mother Orthodox?
cues.zh: 你母亲是东正教徒吗？

cues.en: So I don't even know. My mother...
cues.zh: 所以我甚至不知道。我妈……

cues.en: I I don't I don't know.
cues.zh: 我……我不知道。

cues.en: There was Armenian church, though. There was an Armenian church. Yeah. Well,
cues.zh: 不过有亚美尼亚教堂。有一座亚美尼亚教堂。是啊。嗯，

cues.en: that was a big deal in Worcester, where she came from. In
cues.zh: 那在她来自的Worcester是件大事。在

cues.en: Portland,
cues.zh: Portland，

cues.en: there was an Armenian community,
cues.zh: 有一个亚美尼亚社区，

cues.en: which I think went to an Armenian church or an Armenian dominated church. I'm not sure because that was not my thing. Yeah.
cues.zh: 我觉得他们去的是亚美尼亚教堂，或者亚美尼亚人主导的教堂。我不确定，因为那不是我的事。是啊。

cues.en: And Portland, Maine in the sixties and seventies,
cues.zh: 还有六十、七十年代的Maine州Portland，

cues.en: it was big enough that it... You wouldn't call it a small town. Right?
cues.zh: 它大到……你不会叫它小镇。对吧？

cues.en: How would you describe Portland?
cues.zh: 你会怎么形容Portland？

cues.en: Your community in Portland when you were growing up, was it suburban or
cues.zh: 你成长时在Portland的社区，是郊区还是

cues.en: urban?
cues.zh: 市区？

cues.en: I grew up... We lived in Portland when I was born,
cues.zh: 我长大的经历……我出生时，我们住在Portland，

cues.en: and we moved from Portland to a neighboring town, Westbrook, when I was in second grade. So I was maybe six or seven years old. And Westbrook was definitely the suburbs, even though was only four miles away.
cues.zh: 我二年级时，我们从Portland搬到了邻近的Westbrook。所以我大概六七岁。Westbrook绝对是郊区，尽管离得只有四英里。

cues.en: So I consider myself as growing up in the suburbs.
cues.zh: 所以我自认为是在郊区长大的。

cues.en: And when we got old enough, we had dirt bikes, and we literally drove the dirt bikes a quarter of a mile down the road to where the trails were, and there were trails there.
cues.zh: 等我们够大了，就有了越野摩托车，真的沿着路骑四分之一英里到有林道的地方，那里有林道。

cues.en: And So... It's it's probably worth mentioning. I mean, my brothers and I... I mean, me being more of an academic type person had this exposure to all these things that academics normally don't get exposed to. Like, we'd go dirt bike riding all the time over huge jumps Yeah. You know, doing crazy things. We look back. We don't know how we possibly survived. With my brothers, we literally built a boat.
cues.zh: 所以……这大概值得一提。我是说，我和兄弟们……我是说，我算是比较学术型的人，却接触过学者通常接触不到的东西。比如我们经常骑越野摩托飞过巨大的坡。对。你知道，干些疯狂的事。现在回头看，都不知道我们怎么活下来的。我和兄弟们真的亲手造了一艘船。

cues.en: And it was a high speed boat that went 90 to 100 miles an hour. It's called a drag boat, quarter mile drag boat. And we we we...
cues.zh: 那是一艘时速90到100英里的高速船。它叫直线竞速艇，四分之一英里直线竞速艇。而我们……我们……

cues.en: What for the time would have been called mail ordered a small fiberglass hull from somewhere in California that got shipped out.
cues.zh: 按当时的说法，算是邮购：我们从加州某处邮购了一个小玻璃纤维船体，然后运了过来。

cues.en: Actually, that was our second boat. Our first boat, we literally got plywood.
cues.zh: 其实，那是我们的第二艘船。第一艘船，我们真的就是弄来胶合板。

cues.en: We bought frames,
cues.zh: 我们买了骨架，

cues.en: plywooded it, and fiberglassed it ourselves. That boat probably went 70 miles an hour, and my brother and I were driving in And it one
cues.zh: 我们给船体铺上胶合板，又自己糊了玻璃纤维。那艘船大概能跑时速70英里，我和哥哥正开着它，然后有一次……

cues.en: I looked over the side, and I see it was blue. I see this blue flap,
cues.zh: 我往船边一看，看到是蓝色的。我看到一块蓝色的东西翻了起来，

cues.en: and it was fiberglass starting to come off. And motioned him, so we better go back quickly. And when we got back, it had all ripped off from the bottom just to plywood.
cues.zh: 那是玻璃纤维开始脱落。我向他示意，我们最好赶紧回去。等我们回去时，船底已经全被撕掉，只剩下胶合板。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: it was interesting growing up in a family like that because of all these other experiences that I think most of the people I know today never had anything like it. Yeah.
cues.zh: 在这样一个家庭长大很有意思，因为我有这些其他经历，我觉得今天认识的大多数人都没经历过。是的。

cues.en: And somehow, all survived it. Yeah. And
cues.zh: 不知怎么的，大家都熬过来了。是的。而且

cues.en: in in your school, and I guess in in the in the suburban in Westbrook,
cues.zh: 在你的学校，我猜在Westbrook的郊区，

cues.en: you know, science and technology, did you get exposed to...
cues.zh: 你知道，科学和技术，你有没有接触到……

cues.en: Besides sort of math, was there, you know, would you call... I I guess I would call it
cues.zh: 除了数学之外，有没有，你知道，你会说……我猜我会说

cues.en: sort of fallout from Sputnik. Did did you
cues.zh: 算是Sputnik的余波吧。你

cues.en: have a science education in...
cues.zh: 在学校受过科学教育吗……

cues.en: Yeah. We had a science education and a math education.
cues.zh: 是的。我们受过科学教育和数学教育。

cues.en: You know, we're talking rural Maine now or some... Not way out in the boonies, but we're near Portland, so we've got good teachers. We've got money for the schools.
cues.zh: 你知道，我们现在说的是缅因州乡村，或者某个……不是偏远到荒郊野外，但我们离Portland很近，所以我们有好老师。学校有钱。

cues.en: We've got good schools.
cues.zh: 我们有好学校。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: to to me,
cues.zh: 对我来说，

cues.en: it was a good exposure. Westbrook had a very good school system.
cues.zh: 这是很好的接触。Westbrook有非常好的学校系统。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: today, you go to a lot of schools, and there's all these different lanes and different tracks. And you're on the advanced lane where you're learning calculus
cues.zh: 今天，你去很多学校，有各种不同的通道和不同的轨道。你在高级轨道学微积分

cues.en: as a junior or even earlier sometimes, and the low lanes where you're kind of struggling to get algebra done. We had one lane with some honors classes, and that was it. And that was only in math. We had that in some science too. But I feel I got good, solid exposure to the sciences,
cues.zh: 在三年级甚至更早的时候，而低级轨道上你在艰难地完成代数。我们只有一个轨道，有一些荣誉课程，就这样。而且那只是数学。有些科学课也有。但我觉得我得到了良好、扎实的科学接触，

cues.en: which I liked, and to math, which I liked.
cues.zh: 这是我喜欢的东西，还有数学，也是我喜欢的东西。

cues.en: And I think,
cues.zh: 而且我觉得，

cues.en: maybe more importantly,
cues.zh: 也许更重要的是，

cues.en: I think I was lucky in that the school when I went to high school, actually, in eighth grade, as I preparing was to go to high school,
cues.zh: 我觉得我很幸运，我上高中的时候，实际上在八年级，当我准备要上高中时，

cues.en: the school knew that I had some good math aptitude. And so they kind of singled me out, maybe along with a few other kids, to show us a few extra things and give us extra stuff. So I remember so vividly when I was in eighth grade at the high school orientation,
cues.zh: 学校知道我有些不错的数学天赋。所以他们有点把我挑出来，也许还有几个其他孩子，给我们看一些额外的东西，给我们额外的材料。所以我记得非常清楚，当我八年级参加高中迎新时，

cues.en: they pulled me in and they said, and we have a computer.
cues.zh: 他们把我拉进去，他们说，我们有一台电脑。

cues.en: And I didn't even know what a computer was. Okay? I didn't know what a calculator was, nothing like that. But they had a PDP-eighty.
cues.zh: 我甚至都不知道计算机是什么，对吧？我不知道计算器是什么，完全没概念。但他们有一台PDP-80。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: I didn't know what it did. It was just this box that had some flashing lights. And I just fell in love with it. I'm like, high school's going to be so cool.
cues.zh: 我不知道它是干什么的。就只是一个带几盏闪烁灯光的盒子。我就一下子爱上了它。我心想，高中肯定会超酷。

cues.en: And it was. And so
cues.zh: 确实如此。所以

cues.en: I had teacher. I had the same math teacher for three years, Mr. Small, sophomore, junior, and senior years. He had an advanced honors
cues.zh: 我有个老师。同一个数学老师教了我三年，Small老师，十年级、十一年级、十二年级。他开了一门高级荣誉

cues.en: math class, which I was in. And he would do other things after school
cues.zh: 数学课，我就在那课上。他还会在放学后做其他事情

cues.en: that would enrich us even more. So while we did most of our PDP AD programming after school, kind of come in and use it, right, for as much as you want and throw a handful of us if we wanted to.
cues.zh: 来进一步充实我们。我们大多数PDP-AD编程都是在放学后做的，进来随便用，对吧，想用多久用多久，我们几个人想来的话就一起来。

cues.en: But he would do other things like offer a special class,
cues.zh: 但他还会做别的事，比如开一门特别课程，

cues.en: learn how to programming. We had an Olivetti cash register that could be programmed in some way I can't even remember now.
cues.zh: 学编程。我们有一台Olivetti收银机，可以用某种方式编程，我现在都记不清了。

cues.en: And and so
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: I would get access to all these sort of extracurricular things. So this is... By now, we're in the early seventies, or is this... Well, now you're mid to late seventies. Mid to late seventies. Okay. Yeah. So was the PDPA connected to the outside world with a modem or anything, or was it just a stand alone?
cues.zh: 我能接触到所有这些课外的东西。所以这是……到现在，我们是在七十年代初，还是……嗯，现在是七十年代中后期。七十年代中后期。好的。那PDP-AD是接上调制解调器连到外部世界，还是就一台独立机器？

cues.en: It was a stand alone computer with two ASR 33 teletypes, which is where the normal... The computers... Quote, computer science class... There was no computer science class. There was a math class where you learned a little bit about programming it,
cues.zh: 那是一台独立计算机，配两台ASR 33电传打字机，就是那种普通的……计算机……所谓的“计算机科学课”……根本没有计算机科学课。只有一门数学课，你在那里学一点编程，

cues.en: and you always used just
cues.zh: 而且你一直只用

cues.en: the ASR 30 threes. Right.
cues.zh: 那两台ASR 33。对。

cues.en: But, again, they would let me go after school and load up different things into the computer. So everyone's using basic. I would learn focal.
cues.zh: 不过，他们还是会让我放学后留下来，往电脑里装各种东西。所以大家都在用 BASIC。我还学了 FOCAL。

cues.en: I would learn how to program from the switches on the front,
cues.zh: 我学着用前面的开关来编程，

cues.en: and I would write and and, obviously, my regular basic programs.
cues.zh: 也会写，嗯，当然还有我平常那些 BASIC 程序。

cues.en: But I could just do all these other things just to learn extra stuff that weren't... Wasn't even being taught in class. Focal was lower level or what kind of programming language? Another programming language. I I can't even remember any details, but it was basic like, I think. Yeah. But what what really excited me was programming out the switches. Yeah. You know, you select the address, you select the data, and, you know, load. Yeah. And that was it, and then run when you're done. So is that even... Is that machine or assembler?
cues.zh: 但我还能做所有这些别的事，只是为了学点额外的东西，那些……甚至在课上都不教。FOCAL 是更底层的，还是说它是哪种编程语言？另一种编程语言。我……我连细节都记不清了，但我觉得它有点像 BASIC。对。但真正让我兴奋的是用开关来编程。对。你知道，你选地址，选数据，然后加载。对。就这样，做完再运行。那这算……这是机器码还是汇编？

cues.en: What would you Machine code. Yeah. Machine code. Yeah. You throw it out the bits. You can go. You... Each switch was a bit. Gotcha. Yeah. That was... I that was... I think that was the best. That's good.
cues.zh: 那你会叫它……机器码。对。机器码。对。你把那些位拨出来。就能跑了。你……每个开关就是一个位。懂了。对。那是……我觉得那是最棒的。很好。

cues.en: That... That's great. And so would you call... It was mister Smallwood. Did you think of him as a mentor? Did he take you under his wing kind of? Yeah. Think he did. Yeah. And it was the computer stuff. You know, he sponsored our math team. I became the captain of the math team, had tremendous fun with that. He'd give us all this extra stuff to do outside of class.
cues.zh: 那……那太好了。那你会不会觉得……是 Smallwood 先生。你觉得他是你的导师吗？他有点把你收在门下吗？对，我想是的。对。而且是因为电脑的事。你知道，他赞助我们的数学队。我成了数学队队长，玩得非常开心。他会给我们很多课外额外任务。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: And

cues.en: interestingly, through all this, I thought I was gonna become a statistician.
cues.zh: 有意思的是，经历了这一切，我本以为我会成为一名统计学家。

cues.en: Because I was told
cues.zh: 因为我被告知

cues.en: by... They would have career people come in for career advice, and they said, oh, you guys are really good in math. You're gonna become statisticians.
cues.zh: 职业顾问会来做职业指导，他们说，哦，你们这些人数学特别好，你们会去当统计学家的。

cues.en: And now that would be a perfect career choice because you could have gone right into machine learning and Yes. Repeat that. Yes.
cues.zh: 现在看来那会是个完美的职业选择，因为你可以直接进入机器学习领域。是的，再说一遍。是的。

cues.en: Well, actually, what happened was, I think it was either my junior year or senior year,
cues.zh: 嗯，实际上当时的情况是，我记得是大三还是大四的时候，

cues.en: we got some
cues.zh: 我们得到了一些

cues.en: newfangled
cues.zh: 新奇的

cues.en: data general computer
cues.zh: Data General 计算机

cues.en: that had memory.
cues.zh: 它带有内存。

cues.en: And our our programs could be stored on it.
cues.zh: 我们的程序可以存储在它上面。

cues.en: And this was a whole new paradigm for us programming, and it had a much more advanced BASIC and other ways to interact with it. You could... We could, like,
cues.zh: 这对我们的编程来说是一个全新的范式，它有一个更高级的 BASIC 和其他交互方式。你可以……我们可以，比如，

cues.en: like, real games and stuff on it.
cues.zh: 玩真正的游戏之类的。

cues.en: And I remember,
cues.zh: 我记得，

cues.en: you know, when I got to the school, the PDP-eighty was already installed up and running.
cues.zh: 你知道，我到学校的时候，PDP-8 已经安装好并运行了。

cues.en: But for the data general, it took, like, a week for some technicians to come in and set it up and test it and
cues.zh: 但对于 Data General，大概花了一周时间，几个技术员来安装、测试，

cues.en: do whatever they did. And I... At that point, I said, that's what I'm gonna be. That's gonna be my job. One of those people.
cues.zh: 做了他们该做的事。那时我就说，那就是我要成为的人，那就是我的工作，成为那些人之一。

cues.en: And did it... When you talk about... Did it come with games? Like, was adventure on it, or were there...
cues.zh: 那它……你说到……它自带游戏吗？上面有《冒险》吗，还是有……

cues.en: And were you taken with games at all, or were you more interested just in...
cues.zh: 你对游戏感兴趣吗，还是你更感兴趣的是……

cues.en: This was before adventure.
cues.zh: 那是《冒险》之前的事了。

cues.en: There
cues.zh: 上面

cues.en: was some game on it. I think it was a very basic game
cues.zh: 有一些游戏。我觉得是一个很基础的游戏

cues.en: that would have been a teletype type game. I don't remember what it was, but I did I did love it. Yeah. I did love it. And did math take over your life? I mean, were you a math geek, or were you... Were there other subjects in school that caught your interest?
cues.zh: 应该是电传打字机类型的游戏。我不记得是什么了，但我确实很喜欢它。是的，我确实很喜欢。那数学有没有占据你的生活？我是说，你是个数学极客吗，还是……学校里有没有其他科目让你感兴趣？

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那

cues.en: I guess I was probably a math geek then because the computer science part of it was very minor.
cues.zh: 我想我那时候大概算个数学极客，因为其中计算机科学的部分很少。

cues.en: Although I liked working with the computers much more. Right?
cues.zh: 尽管我更喜欢摆弄电脑。对吧？

cues.en: I also enjoyed some of the sciences. I really liked physics for some reason. Something about that really, really resonated with me. But
cues.zh: 我也喜欢一些理科。不知为何我特别喜欢物理。有些东西真的、真的让我产生共鸣。但是

cues.en: when I went
cues.zh: 当我

cues.en: to college,
cues.zh: 上大学时，

cues.en: then it wasn't about math, it was about computers.
cues.zh: 那就不是数学了，而是计算机。

cues.en: And I went to University of Rochester, didn't offer computer science program, knowing I wanted to do computers.
cues.zh: 我去了罗切斯特大学，它没有计算机科学专业，尽管我知道我想搞计算机。

cues.en: So I was still sort of a, quote unquote, math geek
cues.zh: 所以我当时还算是所谓的数学极客

cues.en: because I had to get a degree in math. That's all they offered. There was no computer science degree. But I spent all my time working on computers. Yeah. And before we leave high school,
cues.zh: 因为我只能拿数学学位。他们只提供这个。没有计算机科学学位。但我所有时间都在搞电脑。是啊。在我们离开高中话题之前，

cues.en: outside pursuits like sports and reading,
cues.zh: 课外活动像运动和阅读，

cues.en: were you a jock at all? Or...
cues.zh: 你算是个运动健将吗？还是……

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: that's
cues.zh: 这

cues.en: an interesting question because
cues.zh: 是个有趣的问题，因为

cues.en: in middle school, of all things, it was all intramural sports,
cues.zh: 在初中，说来也怪，全是校内运动，

cues.en: and I literally played every intramural sport that you could play.
cues.zh: 我几乎玩遍了你能玩的所有校内运动。

cues.en: And I won an award for that in my eighth grade, like most intramural sports played, something like that.
cues.zh: 我八年级时还因此拿了个奖，像是“参加校内运动最多”之类的。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: by the time I got to high school, I wasn't good enough at any of the sports, except for bowling, because we own the bowling alley. Very good bowler. Probably could have become a professional Gallipian bowler.
cues.zh: 等到我上高中时，我在任何运动上都不够好，除了保龄球，因为我们家拥有那个保龄球馆。保龄球打得很好。说不定能成为职业保龄球手。

cues.en: But I wasn't really good enough at the other sports, and I think it was more... I wasn't big enough
cues.zh: 但我在其他运动上真的不够好，我觉得更多是……我体格不够

cues.en: to play the other sports, so I didn't do them in high school other than recreationally,
cues.zh: 去打其他运动，所以高中时除了娱乐性地玩玩，

cues.en: occasionally Yeah. With friends. I then got bigger
cues.zh: 偶尔和朋友一起，我就没怎么参与。后来我变壮了

cues.en: in college for some reasons. My... I had a big growth spurt in college,
cues.zh: 在大学里不知怎的。我……我在大学里猛长了一截，

cues.en: and I'm actually much more athletic now than I was in high school. Right. So never get into sports per se. That having been said,
cues.zh: 而且我现在其实比高中时运动能力强多了。对。所以从来没真正投入过某项运动。话虽如此，

cues.en: my family spent every summer on a lake nearby where we had a summer place, and so I became a very good water skier.
cues.zh: 我们家每个夏天都在附近的一个湖上过，我们在那儿有个度假屋，所以我成了很不错的滑水运动员。

cues.en: And to some people,
cues.zh: 对某些人来说，

cues.en: riding dirt bikes and things like that is very much a sport in that it takes a lot out of you when you're out on trails, and it's bouncing around, and you're hitting jumps, and doing corners, and everything else. So there was that aspect of it.
cues.zh: 骑越野摩托之类的，非常算一项运动，因为你在越野道上会消耗很大，车子颠来颠去，你要飞坡、过弯，还有各种动作。所以它也有这一面。

cues.en: Did your dad's background as a machinist carry over? Did you get into tinkering,
cues.zh: 你爸爸当机械师的背景有没有延续下来？你有没有开始喜欢捣鼓机械，

cues.en: or was there a machine shop at the house? He
cues.zh: 还是家里就有个机加工车间？他

cues.en: had a machine shop at the bowling alley. And we'd always joke it was behind the machines,
cues.zh: 在保龄球馆里有个机加工车间。我们还总开玩笑说，它就在那些机器后面，

cues.en: The front of the house, and then you've got behind the machines. And usually, only time you go behind the machines is to fix them.
cues.zh: 前面是店面，机器后面还有空间。通常你去机器后面，只是为了修机器。

cues.en: He would go behind the machines to build things.
cues.zh: 他会去机器后面做东西。

cues.en: And so he would buy equipment, lathes or, you know, massive drill presses,
cues.zh: 所以他会买设备，车床，或者你知道的，大型钻床，
